evidence.text: The entry labels Warring States forms of the cup graph as 木 with 不 supplying the sound, and identifies short strokes in the cited forms as decorative. It says Qin forms inherit the Warring States writing and sometimes expand 不 with 口 to 否. Its Han forms vary in both the meaning-side shape and sound-side writing. This is the book’s account of graphic development; it does not by itself settle the earliest form or establish that every later variant had the same components.

evidence.text: The entry describes a handled, oval vessel for food from the Warring States through the Han–Jin period and quotes Zhuangzi for 覆杯水. It also gives uses for drinking vessels and measures, including Mencius’s 一杯水, and cites Han-period material. These are the book’s cited examples, not proof of the earliest physical witness or a dated sequence from vessel to measure.

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A01882 杯; explanation, pronunciation, senses, and forms
evidence.text: The dictionary says 杯 is absent from the received Shuowen text. It reports a Shuowen seal-script form analyzed as 木 with 否 as sound, quotes Duan Yucai calling 杯 a vulgar form, and says 杯 later became common. It gives Mandarin bēi and cites the cup sense, a Mencius 一杯水 example, classifier uses, and award-cup uses. Its ancient-character and Han-slip tables report no available data; that is a limit of this dictionary’s tables, not evidence that no early forms exist.
evidence.title: [A01882] 杯 — Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: B01702 桮; received Shuowen analysis and related forms
evidence.text: The 桮 entry quotes the received Shuowen analysis as 木 with 否 supplying the sound and gives 布回切. It treats 桮 as a cup graph related to 杯. This supports reporting 否 as the sound element in that received 桮 analysis; it does not make 否 a demonstrated component of every form of 杯.
evidence.title: [B01702] 桮 — Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 杯 entry; 形義通解 and Guangyun data
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 杯 as 木 with 不 supplying the sound, describes it as an ancient vessel for soup or pouring wine, and cites the received Shuowen analysis of 桮 as 木 plus 否. It gives 布回 for 杯 in Guangyun. This corroborates the distinct scopes of the 不 analysis for 杯 and the 否 analysis for 桮; it does not establish their earliest graphic sequence.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 字頭「杯」

evidence.source: 嚴學宭, “試論古訓的得失與取捨,” 中國語文研究 8 (1986)
evidence.field: PDF p. 2 / article p. 155; discussion of 杯 and 不
evidence.text: The author proposes that 不 can represent a remnant of a felled tree and interprets 杯 as a vessel made by hollowing such a remnant; the article says ancient cups could serve food such as soup. This is an attributed semantic proposal that differs from the sound-component account in 字源. The article’s extracted text around the names of the Shuowen forms is corrupted, so this evidence does not support an exact sequence of printed graph identities.
evidence.title: 試論古訓的得失與取捨

evidence.source: Wiktionary, phonological data attributed to Zhengzhang Shangfang (2003)
evidence.field: 杯 entry; 不 phonetic-series member, Old Chinese Zhengzhang reconstruction
evidence.text: The entry gives 不 as *pɯ, *pɯʔ, and *pɯ' in the same Zhengzhang system used for 杯. Compared with 杯 *plɯː, the forms share a labial onset and rhyme nucleus but differ in the recorded lateral and vowel length. This supports a proposed sound-series relationship; it does not decide whether 不 was phonetic or semantic in the earliest form.

This is a proposed source-bound correction, not an applied repair. The preceding 木-entry prose in the same OCR excerpt belongs to a neighboring entry and should not support 杯 claims.

[SCAN VERIFICATION REQUIRED] 嚴學宭, “試論古訓的得失與取捨,” PDF page 2 / article p. 155, passage beginning “杯”字從“不”: the PDF text extraction corrupts the names of the quoted Shuowen forms. Exact printed glyph identities and their sequence remain unverified; they were excluded from the cited claim. The attempted browser screenshot failed.

The MOE entry reports its own ancient-character and Han-slip tables as unavailable, while 字源 presents forms labeled Warring States. This research did not inspect a named excavated inscription or establish the physical witness date for those forms.

The received Shuowen account of 桮, the 字源 account of Warring States 不 as a sound element, and the article’s semantic hollowed-tree proposal are distinct scoped analyses. Their exact graphic chronology and the role of 不 in the earliest form remain unresolved.

The Mencius and Zhuangzi passages are received textual citations; this research did not establish the dates of their earliest surviving physical witnesses or a chronological path from vessel to classifier or award sense.

The official Unicode Unihan record URLs for 杯, 不, and 否 could not be opened. Although the supplied local reading extract lists their Mandarin values, those rows are not emitted as externally verified evidence, and no current-reading sound array is proposed.

The checkout did not contain sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv. No Baxter–Sagart pairing is used; the cited historical comparison is explicitly limited to Zhengzhang readings reported in the secondary entry.
